utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. I'd just remind counsel that we will sit for two sessions of an hour and a half this morning finishing at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Cvetic. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The affirmation you made to tell the truth still applies. And now Mr. Stamp has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yesterday, Mr. Cvetic, we were speaking about an operation in March 1998 in the Prekaz area and you indicated that the head of one sector at that time, that is RDB, was Jovica Stanisic. Who was the head of the RJB, that is, public security sector, at that time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The public security sector was headed at the time by Vlastimir Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And was there any target of the action who was prominent in the KLA at the time? By target, I mean any personality who was a member of the KLA who was targeted.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in that area of Srbica and Drenica, the Drenica group was active, I mean, the Drenica terrorist group. It was led by Adem Jashari. There were 25 to 30 members of that group.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And do you know what happened to Jashari and the members of his family as a result of that action?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was killed in that operation together with members of his family, not all of them though. If I remember well, his daughter survived. And the senior commanding officers who commanded that operation had first invited civilians to get out and invited the members of the terrorist group to surrender. Around 50 of them did, but those who did not leave the base were mostly killed in that operation. Let me add to what I said yesterday, in that operation in addition to the special operations unit, special anti-terrorist units were involved. Those were the ones that took a direct part in the operation. Their command post was in the ammunition factory located above and overlooking the Jashari Mahala. In the broader area, the zone was secured by two PJP units. The 37th Detachment of PJP from Nis, and the 24th Detachment of PJPs from Pristina. Within that 24th Detachment of PJP, there was also a company of PJP from SUP Kosovska Mitrovica. As the village of Donji Prekaz is within the Srbica municipality, local police from OUP Srbica, the Department of Internal Affairs, was also involved in securing the roads and securing communications. The security detail for the operation itself was from the SUP of Kosovska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you recall the names of the commanders on the ground?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the unit for special operations, the JSO, was commanded by Milorad Lukovic, also known as Legija. The special anti-terrorist unit, SAJ, from Pristina, was commanded by Major Spalovic. The SAJ from Belgrade was commanded by Zoran Simovic, also known as Tutinac. I cannot recall exactly who commanded the SAJ from Novi Sad. I believe it was Mr. Curcic [Realtime transcript read in error "Djordjevic"]. All these special anti-terrorist units, SAJs, from Belgrade, from Novi Sad and from Pristina were led by Zivko Trajkovic who was on site. He directed their work, coordinated activities, and provided instructions. In addition, there was also Goran Radosavljevic, Guri, who at the time was head of the section of PJPs in the city SUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I ask you to pause a minute, please. Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can you hear me? In line 7, the witness said Curcic, C-u-r-c-i-c, and it's misspelled "Djordjevic." He is from Novi Sad. In the sentence that begins with "I believe it was ..." Witness, will you repeat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said I couldn't remember exactly who commanded the SAJ from Novi Sad but I believe he was called Curcic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Continue, please, sorry for the interruption.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you recall approximately how many members of the Jashari family was killed in the course of the action?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly how many members of the Jashari family were killed in that operation; but in total, around 54 persons were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could move on, Mr. Cvetic, yesterday we were discussing the numbers and the fluctuating numbers of policemen in Kosovo and I wanted to show you a document but I couldn't find the part.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we go back to that document. It's 01224.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Look at page 2, third paragraph of page 2. From the first page you can see that this is a summary of the numbers of policemen in Kosovo on 16th of October, 1998, from the MUP. It says a total 14.541 uniformed members of the police force were engaged in Internal Affairs tasks in Kosovo and Metohija. 10.021 are from Secretariats in Kosovo and Metohija, and 4.520 are policemen from other Secretariats in the republic. Have you read that paragraph, Mr. Cvetic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Does that conform to your memory of the situation at that time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I said yesterday that during the anti-terrorist operations that were carried out from the 25th of July until end September, 14.571 policemen were involved in the territory of Kosova and Metohija. But with the arrival of the verification mission and the Holbrooke-Milosevic Agreement, this number was reduced to 10.021. The unit for special operations was withdrawn from Kosovo then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look at page 6 in English. This is an annex to the summary. This is page 5 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This -- can you make it out? Can you see or do you need it to be expanded a little bit? It's a breakdown of the number of police personnel for each SUP. Do the figures, particularly those for Kosovska Mitrovica SUP that you headed, are those figures in accordance with your memory of the situation at the time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if we could just revert or go back to the previous page, the page before the one we are on, page 4 in English. Sorry, page 5 in English, page 4 in B/C/S. No, the B/C/S page was correct just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is an organogram of the Ministry of Interior in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here you can see Secretariats in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, and internal organisational units that are parts of these Secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I just want to ask you one question. You see for Pristina -- under the SUP for Pristina you see SAJ Ajvalija can you tell us briefly what that is and what its connection to SUP Pristina was?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From here we can see that the special anti-terrorist unit is physically located in installations in Ajvalija which is a place near Pristina, but organisationally it belongs to SUP Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender the document and ask that it be received in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received. Is this -- was part of this tendered yesterday? Or is this an entirely new document?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I had shown the witness yesterday, but it was not tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. The whole document will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P1038.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could have a look at P769, and that's document with 65 ter number 4152.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: These are conclusions from a meeting of SUP chiefs and chief of police departments and commanders in PJP on the 26th of October, 1999, chaired by General Stevanovic. Do you recall attending that meeting, Mr. Cvetic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the conclusions represented here, particularly the conclusion in paragraphs 1 and 2, were they given effect?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And this was as, I think, indicated here in pursuant of the November agreements between the KVM and the MUP, or the OSCE and the MUP?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we move on to another issue. You spoke yesterday about some offensive or an offensive that was conducted between July and September, an anti-terrorist offensive. During that period of time, as a matter of fact during 1998, did you see the head of the RJB, General Djordjevic, in Kosovo on official business?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you recall approximately how many times?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Djordjevic was at the meeting of the MUP staff in Pristina on the 22nd July, 1998. Then he took part in an operation that was organised in the area of Malisevo, that was on 28th July. After that, on the 1st of September, he attended another meeting of the MUP staff in Pristina. And in end September he attended yet another meeting when the anti-terrorist operations were finished. On the 5th of November, he was at the MUP meeting in Pristina when the president of the Republic of Serbia, Mr. Milan Milutinovic also came, and at that meeting the interior minister, Vlatko Stojiljkovic, communicated that certain staffing changes occurred in the security forces, and Radomir Markovic was appointed head of the state security sector. I remember these meetings and these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Malisevo is not exactly within your SUP territory. Can you say how you became aware that he was involved in an operation in Malisevo? And just tell us what type of operation it was.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said yesterday that in June and July certain businesses and certain population centres fell into the hands of terrorist groups, and Malisevo was one of them. At the meeting of the MUP staff in Pristina of the 28th July, attended by the interior minister, Mr. Vlajko Stojiljkovic, and the head of that staff, Sreten Lukic; the head of the public security sector, Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic, called in by radio and communicated that he was at the petrol station in Malisevo and that as of that day Malisevo was free. We learned of that at that meeting on the 28th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you also in the course of the operations in 1998 see -- well, let me ask a non-leading question. Were there any other senior MUP officials that had come to Kosovo on official business in 1998? And when I say official business, I mean in relation to operations that would being conducted against the KLA.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Who were the various senior persons who attended in Kosovo for that purpose?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first and foremost, assistant minister, Mr. Obrad Stevanovic attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did he always attend with General Djordjevic or did they attend at different times?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes with General Djordjevic, sometimes independently of him, and sometimes they took turns. General Djordjevic would spend some time at the staff before being replaced by Obrad Stevanovic, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you say "some time," just approximately how long would General Djordjevic stay in Kosovo during that period?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot tell you with any certainty but roughly their stints would be 10 to 15 days. Sometimes a few days more, sometimes a few days less depending on the situation. But I cannot be absolutely exact.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And this was in what period?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in the period in which anti-terrorist operations took place which is between the 25th of July and end of September of 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before we get to 1999, I think perhaps it would be useful if we could discuss briefly the MUP staff. You have mentioned it quite a few times. Can you recall approximately when General Lukic was appointed head of the staff?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Lukic was appointed head of the staff, that is, either of the staff on 11th of June, 1998. And heads of SUPs were informed about this at the meeting at the MUP staff in Pristina by General Obrad Stevanovic. On that occasion, General Stevanovic informed us that there were certain changes in the staff, that the previous leader of the staff, Aco Vasovic, was replaced and that General Sreten Lukic was appointed to this position. The staff of PJPs in Pristina was supposed to be strengthened. In other words, the number of leaders in that staff was to be increased, and for this purpose the decision was made on 11th of June in 1998 to appoint some new people there, and the head of the public security sector signed that decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look briefly at D100.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is a decision on the formation of the staff.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if you go to the next page, you see it's signed by whom?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was signed by the assistant minister department chief, Colonel-General Vlastimir Djordjevic. This is a decision on the formation of the staff dated 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were you familiar with that document? Did you see that document in -- sorry, before we move on, what is the date you see there? I see 15th of May. Perhaps there's a translation issue. It's the 15th of May, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 15th of May, 1998, is the date when this decision on the formation of the staff was made. Decision was made by the chief of the public security sector. And on 11th of June, the decision was made on the appointment of the leader of the staff and members of the staff, and that decision was signed by the same person. But we are talking about two different decisions: decision on the formation and decision on appointments.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let's look at P760. And could we move on to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And is this the decision you just referred to, that is, a decision on the composition of the staff?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you receive or were you shown these documents at about that time in mid-1998?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could move on to P57. This one is dated the 16th of June. Could we move to the next page. Could we move to the last page of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This one is signed by the Minister Stojiljkovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And in paragraph 6 it revokes the two previous decisions to become effective. Did you receive a copy of this one at about that time in mid-1998?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As head of the Secretariat in Kosovska Mitrovica, I did not receive the decision to establish this ministerial staff at that time. And I said that this was signed by the Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic because I can recognise his signature as head of the Secretariat. This is the very first time that I have learned that this particular ministerial staff for the suppression of terrorism was formed. As I said yesterday, I know that back in March a Joint Command was -- a joint intersectorial staff was established for fighting terrorism. And the head of that intersectorial staff, there was Jovica Stanisic, and his deputy was head of public security sector Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic. But this particular decision, this is the first time I'm seeing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we go back to the previous page on both documents, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You'll see after the members of the staff are listed, it says, Expanded staff shall also include chiefs of the Secretariats for Internal Affairs, centres and branches of the RDB in the autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija. Did you consider yourself to be a member of the MUP staff, Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never present at any meeting of this staff which has now been presented to me. I did not even know about this. This is the very first time that I'm seeing the decision on the formation of this staff. And I was present at meetings of the MUP staff in Pristina, but when it comes to this staff for suppression of terrorism established by the minister of the interior, I was never present at any of its meetings. I didn't even know about its existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But if you look at the persons listed here, were these persons in Pristina present and active at the time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here on the monitor I can only see the second page, I cannot see the first page of the document. Of the names listed on the second page -- okay, now I can see the first page as well. All the persons mentioned on the first page were active and these persons also took part in the MUP staff in Pristina. They were members of the MUP staff, and Sreten Lukic was leader of the MUP staff in Pristina. And now I can see that he was also the leader of the staff for the suppression of terrorism. I didn't know that at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let's --

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know all the persons listed on the first page. I know them in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And let's go to the second page to see if you know or not know those listed there.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Some of the persons mentioned on the second page I also know in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, is there anyone there that you do not know was present and working in Pristina or in Kosovo at that time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about them, but I do not know them in person, or actually at this moment I cannot remember them, for example, Radovan Vucurevic and Rasko Milenkovic. All the others I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll get back to the MUP staff later, but if we could move on to another organ or organisation. The operations, the anti-terrorist operations, in July to September 1998 were conducted by which forces, apart from the police?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The anti-terrorist operations that lasted from July until end of September, apart from the police which belongs to the public security sector, there was also a unit for special operations which belongs to the state security sector. Also some other units, units of the Yugoslav Army took part in that operation, which provided support to the MUP units in certain areas in which the operations took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thanks. Was there any body or entity set up to coordinate the activities of the various MUP units and the VJ units that were active on the ground in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you name and describe the functions of this entity, please.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That body was called the Joint Command. In the first half of July, I believe, around the 10th of July, at a meeting of the MUP staff in Pristina, it was stated that a Joint Command was formed. The task of this Joint Command was to coordinate the activities of the army and the police. At the meeting of the MUP staff in Pristina held on 22nd July, 1998, the head of the public security sector stated that a command was established at the highest level and it was to be called a Joint Command. Head of that command was Nikola Sainovic who at the time was vice-president of the federal government. Other members of the Joint Command were Dusko Matkovic, who in the Joint Command was in charge of the economic development that is of starting up different companies and developing the economy in Kosovo. Milomir Minic who was -- who belonged to the socialist party and for a period of time he was general secretary of the socialist party of Serbia, he was in charge of the political issues of working with different organisations and political activities in Kosovo. Another member of the Joint Command was president of the temporary Executive Council, Mr. Zoran Andjelkovic. His task was to coordinate and direct the work of self-management bodies and different district level bodies, that is, municipalities and districts in Kosovo. On behalf of the Yugoslav Army, a member of the Joint Command was the commander of the Pristina Corps, General -- I'll remember his name later on, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: General Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, General Pavkovic. On behalf of the Ministry of Interior, the head of the MUP staff in Pristina took part in the Joint Command, General Lukic; and on behalf of the state security sector, we had a leader of the state security in Kosovo, David Gajic. David Gajic coordinated and directed the work of centres of state security in Kosovo. At the time, there were three of them. And he was at the level of the assistant head of state security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said you were told at a meeting on the 10th of July that it was formed. Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly whether it was General Djordjevic or General Stevanovic, but on July the 22nd it was stated by General Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us what was the role of the Joint Command in exercising its coordinating functions in regard to the MUP staff activities and the police activities, and the VJ?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the anti-terrorist operations for each single anti-terrorist operation, specific plans were drawn so that the police developed their own plans and the army developed its plans. These plans were coordinated, harmonised, at the level of the Joint Command according to different parameters, time, space, and so on. The Joint Command verified these plans and submitted them to the military commanders, PJP commanders, and special anti-terrorist unit commanders, and special operation unit commanders. So all the tasks planned by the police and by the army, they were harmonised at the level of the Joint Command. And as such, they were submitted to the commanders of the units that took part in the operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we have a look at 04057.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is on the face of the document a Pristina Corps Command order to the brigade commanders, and if you look at the second and third paragraphs, it indicates that: "The staff -- the MUP staff of Kosovo and Metohija has issued an order to the Secretariats of the Interior to commence planning actions to crush the terrorist groups that remain in their respective zones of responsibility. To coordinate action with MUP units in crushing the STS, immediately establish contact with SUP chiefs concerning the following:" And they list territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we move to page 2 of the English, and I think we can remain in the same page on the B/C/S document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We see the remaining areas where action was to be planned. Does this represent the way in which the coordinated action of the VJ and MUP were planned? The MUP staff and the Pristina Corps Command would issue orders for meetings to plan these actions?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From this you can see that this was a regular occurrence. However, one can also draw the following conclusion: The VJ specified in great detail the units that took part in particular operations, whereas the MUP forces were not specified to a high degree.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If you look at the planned actions for your SUP area in item 3 and the various sub-items, do you recall any of those actions actually taking place, being planned and executed?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember the Cicavica operation and the Bajgora operation as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Cicavica is at 3.1 and Bajgora is 3.4?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Could this one be received in evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1039, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you see and become familiar with, in your time in Kosovo, the orders, the Joint Command orders for these military operations or actions?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For some I did, for some I didn't. The orders that were submitted to me in which the Ministry of the Interior in Kosovska Mitrovica or the SUP in Kosovska Mitrovica had some duties concerning the execution of these orders; I was informed about them. But I was not informed about other orders issued directly to commanders of different units.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look at 65 ter 01975. That's P969.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That's a Joint Command order for Bajgora?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could the witness be given a copy, I just want to ask him a couple of questions. Mr. Usher, could you?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The previous document is dated the 9th of April, ordering the SUP members and the -- that is, the police members and the brigade commanders of the VJ to meet to plan these operations. Firstly, is this the format of the Joint Command order that you are familiar with? You see on the front page a map of Kosovska Mitrovica. In paragraph 1, a description of the enemy; paragraph 2, the task; paragraph 3, the neighbours; et cetera?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This is the customary military terminology when issuing orders to subordinate commanding officers. Such orders may be issued in the form of orders, instructions, or directives. This is one type of order.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And these were prepared, I take it from your answer, by the Pristina Corps Command?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was harmonised at the level of the Joint Command, and you can see in the left top corner, Joint Command, strictly confidential number, et cetera. But the draft was probably prepared by the Pristina Corps. Let me just mention that there are only minor differences between an order and a decision. The order is a bit broader; it encompasses information about the enemy, neighbouring units, et cetera, et cetera. And the decision begins with what is para 4 in -- in an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could move to page 3 in the English, and in the B/C/S I don't know the page, but that is item 5.1 and 5.3.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: These are the paragraphs or the parts of the order that gives specific tasks to the -- to the units that --

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: For the tasks -- for both of the tasks it says in both 5.1 and 5.3: "Support MUP forces in breaking up and destroying the STS along the following axes." Do you know what MUP units -- can you recall what MUP units were involved in these offensives or tasks?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, this order was taken on the 15th of April, 1999. Let me just see when combat readiness was envisaged by this order, when the units have to be ready. Readiness for communications is 25th April, so it was executed from the 25th of April onwards, and it was taken on the 15th of April, 1999. At that time I was not head of SUP Kosovska Mitrovica because I was relieved on the 16th of April. All my duties and responsibilities at the SUP were taken over by a colleague. So I'm not aware, and I was not interested, which units were involved in this operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we go back to the front page, the first page on the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And for you that is item 2, "Tasks of the Pristina Corps." "With it's reinforcements and the armed non-Siptar population in Kosovo and Metohija, the Pristina Corps shall support MUP forces in breaking up and destroying STS in its zone of responsibility." Can you tell us in one sentence what you understood the armed non-Siptar population to be? This is something we return to later, so we don't need to spend too much time on it now.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not see this in this order, but I can tell you roughly what is understood by that term. But the term itself, I don't see it in these paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you see paragraph 2 in respect to the tasks of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's on page 1, but you said page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, no, I mean paragraph, sorry. Could you just read so we can get a spot translation of that first sentence there.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Pristina Corps with reinforcements and armed non-Siptar population in Kosovo and Metohija, shall support MUP forces in breaking up and destroying Siptar terrorist forces in its area of responsibility." I wouldn't know exactly what this term was understood to mean by the person who drafted this order, but thinking logically, I should think that the Serbian population is meant. And when I say that, I have in mind the following facts: At that time via the Ministry of the Interior and the MUP staff in Pristina, and through Secretariats of Internal Affairs in Kosovo and Metohija, a certain amount of weapons were distributed to the Serbian population. But those Serbs who received the weapons were included in reserve police sections, and reserve police sections had the task of defending their local communes, their villages, their settlements, from various Siptar terrorist forces that were active in the area, that infiltrated themselves into Serbian population centres, and committed arson, looting, kidnapping of people and vehicles, et cetera. That's why it was decided, because of these crimes, to establish reserve police departments and to distribute weapons to the Serbian population. So it is my opinion, therefore, that the non-Siptar population in this text means that segment of the Serbian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we move on to 1968. That's 65 ter number 0968 which is also P971.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is another Joint Command order, I think you'll see there. And the map -- you can see that accompanying it, it's a map of Kosovo or Kosovska Mitrovica. On page 2 in the English --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Perhaps you could hand a copy to the witness again in B/C/S. With the assistance of the usher, could we retrieve the one that he has and give him 1968.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is dated the 24th of April. If you look at the tasks again, you'll see that it is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you mean April, Mr. Stamp, or March?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: March 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: At page 2 of the English, we see the tasks expressed in similar language: "The Pristina Corps with reinforcements of the armed non-Siptar population of Kosovo and Metohija shall support MUP forces in defeating and destroying the Siptar terrorist forces in the zone of its responsibility?" I'd like you to look at paragraph 4, and that's on page 3 in the English, and just tell us, if you can remember, this operation which is to support MUP forces in the area described, and if you can, if you can remember the MUP forces. This is at paragraph 4, the decision.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was head of SUP in Kosovska Mitrovica, I did not receive this order, and I did not see it. This is the first time I'm seeing it. And let me conclude, at first sight, there is something illogical about it. If you allow me to read: The Siptar terrorist forces established the operative zone Drenica with three brigades around 1500 terrorists. And it says, 114th Brigade, 250 terrorists; 112th, 200; and a third one with 400 which -- and another one 300 which makes 700 something. Where do 1500 come from? I can tell you about this only in general terms, but not specifically because I never received this order. I know as the head of SUP that the 37th Brigade of the Army of Yugoslavia was active; the 7th Brigade of the Army of Yugoslavia; PJPs; the unit for special operations, JSO; and anti-terrorist units, SAJs; and the 125th Motorised Brigade from Kosovska Mitrovica. But specifically which units were involved in this operation under which order, I don't know. But generally speaking, the units that I enumerated were active in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And they are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If I could interrupt. We have page 3 on the screen which doesn't include any of the information being read by the witness. Is it page 2 or 4 or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The information is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- at page -- the question was in respect to page 3, whether he recalled this particular action in this area at item 4; but the witness in his answer referred to forces or units that are mentioned at page 4, page 5, page 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can we have pages 4 and then 5 and then 6, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may, I think the question may have been directed to his reference to the mathematics, and that part of his answer is on the first page in English. He gave a rather long answer in which he said that he saw an error in the mathematics, that's on the first page. And then he referred to the units that he knew were operation in Kosovska Mitrovica, that's on page 4, 5, and 6. But if we could look briefly on the first page as well, I think you will see what he says about the addition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, now, did you want to stay something, Mr. Cvetic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did. I was saying that in the area of Drenica at that time, the following VJ, Army of Yugoslavia, forces were operational: The 7th infantry Brigade, the 37th Motorised Infantry Brigade, and 125th Motorised Infantry Brigade. As for MUP units, especially PJP units were involved, I don't know. But PJPs were present. Which particular detachments, I don't know. Special anti-terrorist units and the unit for special operations were also present. From this we can conclude that the two VJ units I mentioned, namely, the 37th Motorised Brigade and 125th Motorised Brigades were involved in these operations. That is, in the execution of the tasks envisaged by this order. That's what I wanted to say, thank you for your permission, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have any objection. The witness has explained everything. But the inferences of Mr. Stamp are wrong. The witness already said he was not aware of this order and he is just telling us which units were present in that area, which means that Mr. Stamp's inferences do not tally with what the witness has said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I haven't grasped Mr. Stamp's inferences yet, Mr. Djurdjic. As usual, you are well ahead of me. Now, Mr. Stamp --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I was asking questions. I didn't mean to infer anything. But I don't want to address on the evidence, the witness has said that he saw some and he did not see some.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. If we could move quickly to a couple more of these Joint Command orders. 02031.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Actually, this is a Pristina Corps order dated the 22nd of March, drafted by the Pristina Corps. A Joint Command order drafted by the Pristina Corps. It's again in your area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could just scroll down in English to the bottom, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think you had made a distinction between the orders which are broader, and the decisions which are narrower. This is a Joint Command decision on the 22nd of March, 1999, in respect to an action in Cicavica. Do you recall this order or this action?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But not concerning Cicavica. This operation whose objective was to engage the main forces on the axis that we see in the order, Poljance, Trstenik, Prelovac, Likosane, which is far from Cicavica; but the point was to prevent spillout and withdrawal of Siptar terrorist forces in Cicavica. And the main axis of attack was as I said, Poljance, Trstenik, and Prelovac-Likosane. The auxiliary axis of attack was Gladno Selo-Likosane and Novo Cikatovo-Trstenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this and ask that it be -- it was admitted P972, I'm told. And the last of these Joint Command orders we look at the for the time being is 04140.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This one is dated the 4th of May, and it's actually a Pristina Corps Command order, and that is after you left. But you recall an earlier order that we looked at today in which there was planning for an operation, you said you remember the operation Bajgora, would this be the order for that operation that was planned while you were there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. I wonder, Your Honours, if this is a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is this already an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. But this -- thank you very much. Could it be received in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1040, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have then the first break now and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, I'd like us to move on to look at events from the standpoint of the MUP as they developed in Kosovo during the relevant period. And in that regard I'd first like to show you this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It's 04151. And the exhibit number is P768 [Realtime transcript read in error "P7568"]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: These are minutes, rather short minutes, consisting of two pages actually, of the MUP meeting held on the 22nd of July, 1998, at the Pristina MUP conference hall. Do you recall attending that meeting, Mr. Cvetic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if you have a look at those persons present, does the list at least at the beginning reflect the relative seniority of the persons present at the meeting? The order in the list, does it reflect the seniority?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: At item 3, we see that Major-General Lukic proposed an agenda that included defining tasks in the implementation of the global plan. What did you understand or what do you understand the global plan to mean, or what would he be referring to there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The global plan was a plan that was prepared for implementation of the anti-terrorist actions that were planned for the 25th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if we could move on to another document, P688, that's 03121.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you tendering this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think it's already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What is the number? Thank you. The transcript showed 7568, clearly not a right number. 768, apparently. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The next document I'd like you to look at is P688.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the 65 ter number is 3121. If we could move to page 3 in both copies, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And these are the minutes of the MUP staff meeting of the 20th of February -- sorry, I beg your pardon, the 20th of July, 1998. I think you had referred to that meeting before in your evidence, and if you look at the --

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- participants, you'll see that you are one of the participants.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In the first paragraph there, in his presentation, Major-General Lukic said that the second part or the second phase of the global plan had been carried out in accordance with the established schedule with ten detachments. Actions were carried out in coordination with the Yugoslav Army, and he stressed that the next task was to liberate and capture Drenica. Could you briefly explain what General Lukic was describing here?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, the plan that was composed to be for the execution of anti-terrorist actions, it included several phases. The first phase was to bring units to the territory, or actually, the first phase was the mobilisation and bringing of the units, PJPs, to the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. On that occasion to the territory of -- in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, there were ten detachments of PJPs that were stationed at various Secretariats throughout Kosovo and Metohija. The bringing of these forces required the next phase, and this is was accommodation and deployment of personnel, of forces, their learning about the plans, and specific tasks for each single unit. So the first phase completed, this means that mobilisation was completed, that forces were brought there, and that the units learned about the tasks of respective units; and now they were supposed to move to the second phase of this plan. Obviously I do not have this plan in front of me right now, so I cannot be entirely certain in claiming what this second phase is supposed to be. But most probably, this was the implementation of the specific tasks as specified by the global plan, give that the first two phases were completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could now move on to page 7 in the English, page 8 in the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And I see you made a presentation there. But what I'd like you to focus on for the time being is what was said by Captain Pesic, Captain Blagoje Pesic, did you know him before? Or could you tell us who Captain Pesic -- Captain Pecic was at the time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as you can see here, it was captain Blagoje Pesic and he worked at the staff of PJPs. His task was to plan, organise, and train reserve police units. I knew him in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And do you recall him making the presentation that we see represented here about the reserve police station? Well, first, could you just tell us, we see here that he says: "We formed 243 reserve police stations." That is what we have in the English translation. But these RPOs, are they reserve police stations with fixed buildings or offices or are they reserve police detachments or units which was a word you used earlier? Could you just explain what an RPO is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I'm not sure what the transcript says, but I hear the interpretation as reserve police stations and the witness talked about reserve police departments or units, so this is a very large difference because the police station is an institutional formation and reserve police department or unit is something very different. So when we are talking about departments or squads rather --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The question, Mr. Djurdjic, is asking the witness to explain more precisely what was meant, so your uncertainty may be clarified by the answer. Thank you. Do you remember the question, Mr. Cvetic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. The first thing I would like to say is that indeed Captain Blagoje Pesic at this meeting talked about the training, or sorry, about the formation of reserve police units and possible problems expected with their formations, so he informed us about what was done up to that moment as regards the formation of reserve police squads or units. Let me explain what these reserve police squads are. In June of 1998 at a meeting of the MUP staff in Pristina --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, we are going to get into these squads in more detail later. I just wanted to clarify for the time being that the RPOs are reserve police squads, that's what it refers to?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. This is personnel that was formed or established in every single village, in every single inhabited area, to protect their inhabited area. They were formed following military conventions, so they had a commander, deputy commander, and a certain number of members. But they were not permanently mobilised. They did not have a separate venue or facility, and they did not function as an organisational unit. So they only became an organisational unit at the time when they were mobilised to defend their village from the attack launched by the Siptar terrorist forces. And after the end, they all left to their respective homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We have here an acronym in the English translation that we are using: RPO. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means reserve police squads.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll get to those squads in more detail later on. Was this the meeting you were at when General Djordjevic called to report on the action in Malisevo?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was at the meeting at the MUP staff in Pristina on July the 28th when General Djordjevic called in via radio transmitter and stated that he was at a petrol station in Malisevo, and that as of that day, Malisevo was free. This was what was conveyed to us, and I'm not aware that he reported on anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could move on to document 02528. Perhaps if we could look at the second page in B/C/S. We could remain on the first page in English, or we could look at the second page in English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is a dispatch sent by the head of the MUP staff of the 21st of October, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if we could go back to the first page. Item 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were these instructions you received from General Lukic on how to receive and deal with the KVM monitors?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were not only instructions issued by General Lukic, but this was the position of the Ministry of the Interior, or actually, the position of the state politics of the Republic of Serbia, and it was merely conveyed through the ministry staff to us. So after the arrival of the mission to Kosovo and Metohija, after Milosevic-Holbrooke Agreement was signed, there were some 2.000 verifiers in the area of Kosova-Metohija, and we got instructions on how to treat representatives of the OSCE mission, instructions on our mutual contacts, exchange of information, and so on. So, yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think you are saying that the MUP staff was a conduit for these instructions which came from high up, from the ministry itself?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I said, the MUP staff served as an intermediate command which linked the ministry and lower ranks. So the information coming from the ministry when sent to the Secretariats in Kosovo were sent via MUP staff, usually. Although sometimes we also received information directly from the ministry; it all depended on the type of information. But this particular information came from the MUP staff in Pristina to heads of Secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if we scroll down a little further, I think you want page 2 in the B/C/S, we could have a look at item B on the front page in English, and then move on to the second page in English as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The obligation to report, as mentioned here by General Lukic, was this mandatory and was this complied with?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a type of methodological instruction that was submitted to the heads of Secretariats, and it considered the way in which they should treat the representatives of the OSCE mission and what is it that they should report on to the staff. As a Secretariat, we were obliged to fully comply with everything that is listed here, not only this, but we were also obliged to receive OSCE mission, to accommodate them, to guarantee their full safety and to cooperate fully with the OSCE mission. We were obliged to exchange information with them on a daily basis. And as a head -- as the head of a Secretariat in my own facility in my own office, I received OSCE mission representatives and informed them about all the significant events and occurrences. They also asked for certain security related problems in Kosovo to be resolved in accordance with the law and in accordance with what was agreed within the Milosevic-Holbrooke Agreement. Apart from me, the authority to be in touch with the OSCE mission was also given to commanders of the police stations and also personnel working at check-points, so police officers working at intersections, traffic police, they could also be in conduct with OSCE mission representatives. But it was clearly stipulated which level could share what type of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, could this one be received and given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P1041.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could move on to have a look at another document very quickly, this is P770, 65 ter number 02805. And we could move straightaway to page 3 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: These are minutes of a meeting held on the 5th of November, 1998, at the ministry staff in Pristina, and it was attended by various leading figures in the republic at the time. Do you see the attendees of this meeting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you recall this meeting? Did you attend this meeting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the minutes here indicate that the president of the republic, Mr. Milutinovic, made a presentation in respect to your obligations under the Milosevic-Holbrooke Agreement. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was given in 11 points.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We could move on to another document P689. And it's 65 ter number 03122. And we could go straight to page 3 in both. These are minutes of the meeting of the ministry staff, chiefs of the SUPs, and commanders of the detachments of the Special Police unit on the 2nd of September, 1998, in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, the 2nd of December, 1998, in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am sorry, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And do you recall attending this meeting --

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can remember this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If you look at the first paragraph, you'll see that Major-General Lukic made a presentation in which he said that, and I'll just read it: "That on the 27th of November, 1998, in Belgrade a meeting of the Ministry of Interior which was chaired by Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic was attended by the chiefs of the departments of the JB, that is public security, and the DB, state security, assistant ministers, head of the MUP staff in Pristina, and Nikola Sainovic."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please read a bit slower for the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Pardon me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: "The current security situation in Kosovo was examined in the meeting in which the duties and further engagement of members of the police in Kosovo were defined. The essence of the meeting was to continue execution of anti-terrorist actions aimed at suppressing terrorism in Kosovo, and that in this regard the police will be more offensive in taking measures in the newly-arisen situation." Firstly, did General Lukic frequently brief the heads of the organisational units in Kosovo about meetings that he had with the police leadership in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. When he had meetings he would sometimes, depending on the topic, say that he had just been at the meeting in the Ministry of Interior and he would share with us what had been said, sometimes not, depending on the topic of the meeting and whether there was any need to inform heads of Secretariats. It was up to his judgement. Sometimes he would inform us, sometimes he would not. How many times he attended meetings at the ministry and what was discussed at those meetings, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Now, having regard to the first paragraph, the part I just read about the persons who attended this meeting, and what was the purpose of the meeting and the topics discussed, can you comment based on your knowledge as to who were the top decision-makers within the police force on the use and engagement of police units in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the decision to engage the police in suppressing terrorism in Kosovo was made only at the level of the Ministry of Interior. The decision was made by the minister and his closest associates, or perhaps sometimes by a person authorised by the minister. When PJP units were to be sent to Kosovo, it was usually head of the public security sector who gave the authorisation. He was the one who made the decision to send police to perform security tasks in Kosovo. But the command over those units was exclusively in the hands of unit commanders. Once the decision to send and engage units in security tasks in Kosovo was made, specific tasks to those units were given also by the MUP staff in Pristina as the body directly on the ground that had an insight into the overall security situation. And it was based on this assessment of the overall security situation that the MUP staff issued tasks to SAJ units and PJPs, but not to the JSO because they had no command over them. And the execution of these tasks was exclusively within the purview of the unit commander who had command in a particular area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we look at page 8 in the English and page 7 in the B/C/S. Are we there? Could you scroll down to the bottom of page 7 in the English copy. It's end of the document in both.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We see here that Lukic -- General Lukic, or Mr. Lukic, gave instructions for the commanders present to submit a plan for the prevention of terrorism in their areas. I'm just trying to get a better understanding of the chain of command from the ministry in Belgrade to the units on the field in Kosovo. And what I'd like to ask, as a result of this instruction, were activities planned on the ground level, that is, by units operating on the ground or heads of units operating on the ground in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, operations in the combat against terrorism have a two-pronged role. There are two types of operations: offensive and defensive. In this specific case that we see on this page and that is specified in the plan on fighting terrorism, this plan is basically a plan of defence, a plan to defend population centres and territory, and to enable free passage and traffic of people, goods, and communications. This part of the plan was taken care of by Secretariats of the Interior. However, offensive plans drafted at the level of the ministry and the army and that were harmonised at the level of the Joint Command, they were then handed down to units that were to execute them. So those are offensive plans. And this plan is defensive for contingencies such as defending yourself from terrorist attacks. And you can see from the paragraphs that it is a plan of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could move on to document 03116. It's a document dated two days later, the 4th of December, 1998. 3116.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Perhaps you refer to 2166, Mr. Stamp. I can't open 3116.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: 3116, I think. May I just have a moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It's maybe -- I don't know if it will help if I say 03116. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This draft plan of the Internal Affairs organs in Glogovac for -- to prevent terrorism, 4th of December, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If you could just go to the end of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We see that there's an area for the signature of the chief of the Secretariat, Colonel Petric, Colonel Bosko Petric. Who was Colonel Bosko Petric? Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know him. Bosko Petric was the chief of SUP in Pristina at the time, and he was chief of SUP in Uzice before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: To the right of that you see that the plan was made by the chief of OUP, Major Petar Damjanac. Who was he? Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: OUP Glogovac was organisationally part of SUP Pristina. This plan was drafted by the chief of the OUP Internal Affairs department in Glogovac, whom I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But do you know the name Petar Damjanac, or did you know the name at that time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the name is familiar, but I don't know the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And this is a plan prepared, I take it, in response or in compliance with the previous document we had seen, the instructions from General Lukic of the 2nd of December?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. So on the basis of these documents, could you just tell me if my understanding of what you are saying is correct, that the leadership of the police including the Minister Stojiljkovic; the chief of the RDB, Mr. Markovic; the chief of the RJB, Mr. Djordjevic; and other senior members like the assistant ministers would formulate the policy and define the task and the engagement of the police, and that was conveyed sometimes to the SUPs directly, and sometimes to the ministry staff? In this case with these documents General Lukic and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a direct examination. This broad question contains a number of inferences by Mr. Stamp. I know this witness cannot be easily misled, but I believe it would be more appropriate to answer proper -- to ask and answer proper questions. Mr. Stamp in his question has already concluded what is done at what level and how it is executed, and now he wants the witness to confirm. And by the way, the witness answered two questions ago exactly how decisions and plans were made. This is a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is a leading question, Your Honours, but this question arises from evidence already given by the witness and how the documents are to be interpreted, and I'm merely asking him if the summary I give of his evidence and the documents is correct. It is leading question, but it is based on the evidence that has already been given and the natural meaning of the words in the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, you are doing two things, Mr. Stamp. You are bringing into the answers contents of documents that have not been the subject of specific oral evidence so far. So you are not merely summarising what the witness has said, you are summarising documents that have been tendered and what the witness has said. I am afraid that's a step too far.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honours. I will accept that and move on, Your Honours, so that we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The question is gone, Mr. Djurdjic. Your objection has been successful. As ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How will you explain, Mr. Cvetic, or relate plans formulated by the units or the groups on the ground in Kosovo to the decision-making by General Djordjevic and the minister in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your suggestion was not successful, Your Honour. Mr. Stamp again concluded himself who made plans in Belgrade. Let me just remind you that the witness said decisions were made by the minister or a person authorised by the minister. Those decisions were handed down to Kosovo where they were executed by the commander, and specific tasks were issued by the staff. Now, Mr. Stamp should say what type of plan he means in his questions, because there is a number of plans.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, you have introduced into your question a very big factual disputed matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You may want to ask how were decisions made at the ministry implemented, but you come to the point of introducing specific decisions of the accused and the minister without distinction.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, but I think the witness testified about those. However, I will withdraw the question and I think, as usual, the way it is formulated by Your Honours is perhaps the best way to go about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How were decisions made at the ministry level by either the minister himself or the chief of the public security department implemented by the forces on the ground in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be specific in answering this question, I would kindly ask you to specify your question to a higher degree. Do you mean to ask decisions only taken during the anti-terrorist actions, or during the state of immediate threat of war, or the war? Or you mean the overall period in Kosovo? If you mean the overall period in Kosovo, each ministry developed its own programme of work which was an annual programme. That annual programme specified concrete tasks in every area of security work. That programme, or rather, it's extract was delivered to each of the 33 Secretariats on the territory of Serbia. And based on that plan, based on that programme, each Secretariat would develop its own plan for the following year, specifying their objectives, how to attain them, specific tasks and who was responsible for them. Specifically, if you want to know about the events that triggered anti-terrorist actions or the events that followed the immediate threat of war situation, you would find decisions that say that the decision was made exclusively by the minister or a person authorised by the minister. As a rule, the authorised person was head of the public security sector. Why do I say that? Because I personally held dispatches on the sending of units to Kosovo and Metohija to perform special security tasks, and they were signed by the head of the public security sector General Djordjevic. Now, speaking of the execution of such decisions, the decision to engage units is one segment in the chain of control. Another segment is command. Command was within the exclusive purview of the executing units. But how did they command? They commanded on the basis of plans previously made at the level of MUP staff and at the level of the army. These plans were harmonised at the level of the Joint Command. And then in the form of orders or decisions, they were handed down to units on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not an objection, Your Honour. In line 19 -- sorry, page 19, line 15 and 16. It wasn't recorded that it was the minister of person authorised by the minister who made decisions to send. I was mistaken about the page number, the page number is 40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm not sure what your concern is. What I have recorded indicates that decisions would stipulate if they were made exclusively by the minister or by a person authorised by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but what is missing is that those were decisions to send.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, you might clarify that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What sorts of decisions were you referring to in your answer in respect to the anti-terrorist action in Kosovo? What sort of decisions by the authorities in Belgrade were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, the people that I mentioned who were at the top of the pyramid of the ministry in Belgrade, the minister, heads of sectors, and even certain assistant ministers, took the decisions to send units. They write this decision in the form of dispatch. This dispatch is sent to Secretariats. And it says that on such and such a day and such and such an hour they should send such and such a unit somewhere on the territory of the Secretariat. It is further specified which vehicles they will use, what kind of weapons they will take, et cetera. That's the decision sent in the form of dispatch. Now, the other decision to execute combat operations is something entirely different. Nothing to do with the first type of decision. That decision is taken at the level of the MUP staff in Pristina and the army. It is then harmonised at the level of the Joint Command, and it's an entirely different type of decision that specifies the tasks of combat units in specific operations in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you have mentioned these decisions, maybe we could look at a couple of documents and ask you what they are about.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look at 4134 quickly, please. And it's P138.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you mean to tender --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I'm so sorry. Sorry. Could this one be received in evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 3116 will be Exhibit P1042.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is a MUP dispatch of the 18th of March, 1998, to SUP chiefs and PJP detachment commander, and I think you can see on your copy that it is signed for the chief of the public security department General Djordjevic. It's probably self-evident from the face of the document, but can you tell us briefly the purpose of this document? What is this about?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the right question. This is the decision to send units to carry out special tasks in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija in the form of a dispatch, and it regulates all the issues that I previously mentioned. And here you can see that it was signed by head of the public security department, so this is the way in which the heads of Secretariats received orders, through this kind of dispatch. And then also at the ministry level, such dispatch could be signed by a different person who was authorised by chief of the public security department. And usually it would be the person in charge of these particular types of units. That person would sign a dispatch as authorised by the head of the public security department, it would be submitted to the communications centre, and communications centre would forward it. And the heads of the Secretariat were informed to prepare their -- and organise their units and send them on such and such a date to such and such a place. The same is true when it comes to withdrawal of units from Kosovo and Metohija for a period of rest. Usually they stayed in Kosovo for 40 days and after that they would be replaced or withdrawn. So here you can see that this dispatch was not signed by General Djordjevic but it was signed upon his authorisation which was a regular practice at the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just as another example, if we look briefly at 4135. That is 04135, which is P139. If we could just look at the front page and then the next page quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That's another example of what you just described, Mr. Cvetic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And all such dispatches that I could see were written following the same methodology.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. To round off this area, may I -- could we go back to this document P689. This is 03122. Page 3 in both Serbian and English versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And again referring to the briefing by Mr. Lukic about the meeting he attended in Belgrade on the 27th of November, 1998. If you could read that first paragraph again and --

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: My question may be a little obvious, but I'll ask it anyway. What sort or types of decisions were made at these meetings, the meeting that Mr. Lukic described?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lukic here described the situation which was analysed by the Ministry of the Interior together with heads of public security sector and state security sector, and attended -- this meeting was attended also by Mr. Sainovic. The situation analysed by the MUP staff in Pristina is an overview of the security situation in all the Secretariats. So the current topics and problems are discussed and what needs to be done in order to raise the security level. All heads of Secretariats and all commanders of PJP detachments describe the situation in their respective territories, that is, in their Secretariats; and commanders of other units, for example, special anti-terrorist units, would describe the situation this their units, the situation and the problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What I'm asking is this: The meeting involving Mr. Stojiljkovic, Mr. Djordjevic, Mr. Markovic, Mr. Sainovic, what types of decisions were made at these meetings?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At these meetings, decisions were not made. They simply analysed the situation, and then later on this was transformed into certain conclusions, and these conclusions were incorporated into certain plans for the engagement of units. This is my understanding of the issue. I am not sure if I was clear enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, I think it's probably that I'm not understanding or I didn't understand what you meant when you say they analyse the situation and then this was transformed into certain conclusions. Would you explain that further what you mean, They analyse the situation, it was transformed into conclusions which are incorporated in plans.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, the political and security situation was analysed and there was a very specific methodology whereby the political and security situation was described on the basis of an analysis of the political security situation, conclusions were drawn. And on the basis of these conclusions, specific tasks were made which were then incorporated into plans for individual units.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could move on to another document, 3130. And that is P690. This is another MUP staff meeting. I think we could move straight to page 2 of this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: These are the minutes of the MUP staff meeting of the 3rd of November, 1998. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we have page 2 of the B/C/S as well, please. Or, it's page 3 of the B/C/S, I'm so sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you recall this meeting, Mr. Cvetic? Did you attend it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And I see here it says: "Following the speech of the chief of the Secretariat."
