I think there is a mistake there, it think it should be the chief of the staff, "the following conclusions were adopted," and number 1 was that: "The basis of your activities is a report by the president of the Republic of Serbia, Milan Milutinovic. In respect to various discussions as well as the agreement signed by Colonel-General Vlastimir Djordjevic and the head of the USA Diplomatic Mission Mr. Shaun Byrnes?" Do you remember those discussions and those conclusions at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I can just state that this is okay. After the speeches of the chiefs of the Secretariats, not after the speech of General Lukic. General Lukic chaired the meeting. He greeted everybody present and gave the floor to chiefs or heads of Secretariats so that they could describe the situation this their respective areas. And pursuant to these reports, certain conclusions were drawn. This is what I previously stated. So this is one example of how these conclusions were drawn on the basis of the analysis of the situation. So yes, I can recall this meeting and whatever is stated here is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we move on to page 3 of the English. That's page 4 of the B/C/S. Item 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If you could just comment on it, help us to understand what was being -- what this conclusion meant and if it had an effect.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This conclusion is quite all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, when it says at the end: "Commanders and deputy-commanders will take command of the dispatched units - "A" units of the PJP - and all units will come under the Secretariats." What does that mean, and did these PJP units come under the Secretariats thereafter?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not what these conclusions say. These units were not -- they could not be -- and if anybody wanted to put them under command of Secretariats, this could not be effected. The Secretariat when it comes to PJPs had the following tasks: First of all, to accommodate PJPs in the facilities, so to provide accommodation, to provide food, health care, sanitation; to secure necessary number of vehicles, if needed, by PJPs; also to secure weapons so that whatever was used up could be replaced; and so on. So these were the functions of the Secretariats as regards the PJPs. So simply to provide logistics. Within the command system, it is clearly stipulated who commands which units and who can make decisions on the use of particular units, and you cannot make any decision that would change that. And this -- these conclusions certainly are not doing that because the commanding and functioning are two very different things. Let me explain. Commanding is one part of controlling, and functioning of the Secretariat simply means carrying out the tasks as stipulated by the Law on the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thanks for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could move on to item 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I could read from about the middle of that item: "Make sure that Serbs and members of the RPO" - properly translated here as reserve police squads - "do not misuse weapons, let off guns at weddings, celebrations of Slava, farewell parties, and so on. Do not carry weapons or show them in public in the presence of members of the mission. When on guard duty, use one weapon and prevent individuals from bringing in the weapon they have been issued. Tell them not to state the fact that the Serbs are armed and to explain this fact, if they must, using the excuse that it is only members of the guard who are armed." Was this one of the conclusions that was drawn at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was there a particular reason to -- or not to reveal to the mission, the KVM mission, the degree to which the Serb population was armed?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, there was no justified reason for this because it was done publicly, that is, through the public security sectors, through the staff and Secretariats, so everybody knew about this. Serbs were issued weapons to protect their villages, to defend their villages, so to protect themselves and to defend their villages from the entry of the Siptar terrorist forces. And the weapons could only be used for these purposes. However, there were occasions when weapons were misused by the Serbs. They would fire off weapons at weddings, different religious facilities, and so on; so whatever is list is here is absolutely correct. Certain measures were taken against some individuals. The weapons were taken away from some people and later on returned. When it comes to the OSCE mission, there was no reason to hide from them that Serbs were armed. But they were armed through reserve police squads, and this was also legitimate, covered by an instruction adopted at the level of the ministry which was to form reserve police squads at level of inhabited areas, and to issue arms weaponry to the population there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And that is your opinion, I take it, so therefore you didn't agree necessarily with the concealment of this -- of the degree to which the Serbs were armed -- or very well, the question is withdrawn. Could I just check one --

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. To be more specific, there was no reason to hide anything. We were supposed to provide all the information to the OSCE mission. This was a verifying mission, and the goal of all of us of the political structures at Kosovo as well were to carry out the decisions of the top leaders of the state, and this was to present all the facts to the OSCE mission so that they can determine what could be a proper solution for the problems in Kosovo. So for that reason, no hiding was necessary, and why some people decided to hide some things, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we move on to document 0991. This is a MUP meeting of the 21st of December. Sorry, 01991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That last document is already an exhibit, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The last one, 3130, it is an exhibit. Yes, Your Honours, it is 690.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I wonder if it's a convenient time because I will probably spend some time on this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will adjourn now as indicated to resume tomorrow morning at 9.00. You are watching your total time, I take it, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will have to, it seems, beg the leave of the Court to go somewhat beyond it, it seems, at the rate we are going. But we'll try to make it up, -- we can make it up with other witnesses that we could shorten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We encourage you and give you great strength in your task of going quicker, and Mr. Djurdjic will have the same encouragement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But we recognise some things are important and need to be covered. We must now adjourn again, sir, because of a special need. We will continue tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 1st day of July, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.
